text:
maria: Heads-up: did a long-run perf sweep across Hosted / Dedicated / Private for kv-cache behavior with long contexts. Seeing steady memory growth on Private after ~30m, but Dedicated looks stable. Thoughts?

ajay: Can you paste the profiler output? is this KV-residency or just overall RSS growth? :thinking:

maria: It's KV-residency primarily. Short dump below (trimmed):

```
# private-onprem run @ 30m
kv_slots_total: 72M
kv_slots_used: 63.5M
kv_evictions/sec: 0.02
page_faults/sec: 18
rss: 38.3G

# dedicated run @ 30m
kv_slots_total: 72M
kv_slots_used: 59.2M
kv_evictions/sec: 1.4
page_faults/sec: 1
rss: 30.1G
```

maria: Note the low evictions/sec on Private despite high used slots -> looks like paging/fragmentation preventing reclaim.

chen: Did you run with the same jemalloc/tcmalloc build? onprem images are still using jemalloc-5.2 in that fleet, hosted/dedicated use patched tcmalloc. jemalloc can coalesce differently and keep pages mapped.

maria: Good call. Private image is older. I also noticed the kernel fallback path picks a different MatMul kernel on Private which increases per-token mem transiently. Might be compounding with allocator differences.

rachel: Also remember VPC MTU on Private cluster is 1400 vs 9000 in Dedicated — we've seen packetization causing more RPC fragmentation for the offload path. Could that delay KV eviction signals?

dan: That's subtle but plausible. If the KV invalidation RPCs are delayed, the local eviction policy may not see remote frees and end up keeping frames pinned. Any logs for RPC latency?

maria: Yeah snippets:

```
[2026-02-14T15:22:10Z] kv-invalidate: peer=10.0.5.12 latency=3ms
[2026-02-14T15:22:10Z] kv-invalidate: peer=10.0.6.21 latency=120ms <-- Private region
```

maria: That 120ms spike happens during bursts. Combined with a conservative batching heuristic on Private (we defaulted to batch_size=8 there to keep latency) we end up with many small batches that create more unique KV frames and fewer reuse opportunities.

ajay: So two axes: allocator+kernel differences + RPC/batching causing fragmentation and lower reuse. How reproducible is this if you swap allocator on Private to our patched tcmalloc?

maria: I tried a quick container with tcmalloc and re-ran a 45m test — KV_used plateaued ~58.8M and rss dropped ~6GB relative to jemalloc. Will run a longer one tomorrow.

chen: If that's true, we should also try forcing the kernel selector to the same kernel used on Dedicated (there's a flag in runtime/exec: --force-kernel=/kernels/fast-attn-v3). Might remove the transient per-token overhead.

maria: Doing both in next run. Also logging a hypothesis: page-aligned slab fragmentation on older drivers + small batch churn => pages stay split and never consolidated, so reclamation marks them cold (pagefaults) instead of freeing.

rachel: Can we flip VPC MTU to jumbo on a staging Private node? would prove the RPC fragmentation angle quickly. Ops? ops-bot any chance to flip MTU on test VPC for a 2h window?

ops-bot: @rachel I created a change request CR-9876, scheduling network window 2026-02-15 03:00-05:00 UTC for mtu=9000 test on staging-private. Please confirm rollback plan.

rachel: Confirmed rollback plan: revert to 1400 if any regression in inter-service latency > 10ms.

dan: Also cc-ing infra: can we get GPU drivers on Private fleet bumped? older drivers (470.x) may not support the kernel memory reclaim hints the runtime uses (madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) semantics differ).

maria: Filed infra ticket INF-3242 to test nvidia-driver 525+ on a canary node.

ajay: One quick ask: add a micro-benchmark to repro pattern where many short unique prefixes create high slot churn. We need a clean test that isolates batching vs kernel vs allocator.

maria: Will add micro-bench to perf harness: 1) synthetic short-burst workload (batch_size=2-16), 2) long-context reuse workload (seq_len=8k), 3) toggle kernel/allocator flags. I'll post artifacts.

chen: If we confirm allocator is dominant, we can either standardize tcmalloc on Private or add a slab coalescer in the KV layer to reduce fragmentation. Slab coalescer could be faster to ship.

maria: Logged an RFC note with initial results on the perf board. Short summary: Private (old drivers + jemalloc + small batches + smaller MTU) -> higher pagefaults and KV growth. Dedicated (new drivers + tcmalloc + larger batches) -> better reuse and lower rss.

rachel: Great. If you need ops help to run longer tests, ping me. :eyes:

maria: Thanks. Next steps: run tcmalloc+kernel-forcing on Private, run MTU trial, and long 4h run with microbench. I'll update thread with raw traces and the perf compare table. :party:
